_about: PurTera's fixed handling per job type: SOW items a PM writes on every job of that type whether or not the deal states them (template content, not deal facts). Owner-reviewed. The writer writes every item unless a deal fact contradicts it. Sections match sow_method_library.json.

decommission_packing._source: owner, 2026-10-18 (010115 v1 grade: PM-habit items are PurTera standard handling); items added from the 010115 v1 TEMPLATE list (grade round 12)
method_steps: Meet the onsite contact on arrival and review the hardware to be dismantled and packed.
Assist with the physical disconnection of the equipment as directed by the onsite contact.
Dismantle the hardware and organize it for packing.
Pack the equipment in the customer-provided boxes and packing materials, labeling each box.
Package the equipment as instructed by the customer's representative.
Place the packed equipment in the customer's designated staging or shipment area.
Notify the onsite contact of any damage, missing materials or access issues.
Maintain a clean and orderly work area and remove packing debris.
Confirm completion with the onsite contact before leaving site.
customer_responsibilities: Identify all hardware in scope for dismantling and packing.
Ensure the onsite contact or designated representative is available throughout the engagement.
Provide sufficient packing materials (boxes, pallets, tape and labels) onsite before the technician arrives.
Designate a staging or shipment area for the packed equipment.
Provide packing and labeling instructions for the equipment.
Provide any additional security, dock or escort requirements before arrival.
Disconnect or arrange for the safe disconnection of any electrical, building, security, or specialized connections that require a licensed trade or manufacturer-authorized resource.
Accept responsibility for the transportation, shipment, storage, and disposal of all equipment and materials.
Ensure equipment is accessible and free from obstructions.
Provide any specialized tools, carts, pallets, shipping or lifting equipment the job needs.
assumptions: Equipment is powered down and released for removal before the technician arrives.
Onsite parking is available; any parking fee is reimbursable.
The engagement is limited to onsite physical labor and smart hands support.
The hardware can be safely dismantled using common hand tools.
No specialized lifting equipment or powered material handling equipment is required.
exclusions: Transport, shipping or freight of packed equipment.
Hardware installation, configuration, programming, troubleshooting, data migration, network changes, or system testing.
Inventory audit, asset reconciliation, disposal, recycling, data destruction, or certified IT asset disposition.
deliverable_outcomes: Hardware dismantled as directed by the onsite contact.
Equipment packed in customer-provided materials and labeled.
Packed equipment staged in the designated shipment area.
Damage, missing materials or access issues reported to the onsite contact.
Completion confirmed with the onsite contact.

pos_install_refresh._source: owner standards loop 2026-10-18: generic POS handling common to the 000123 and 010198 v1 TEMPLATE lists (device-specific steps left to the deal)
method_steps: Confirm the installation locations and identify the register lanes in scope with the onsite contact.
Verify that the required equipment, power and network connectivity are available before beginning installation.
Perform cable management and organize unused cabling as reasonable within the allotted onsite time.
Perform functional testing of each installed device before leaving the site.
Clean the immediate work area of installation packaging and loose cabling created by Provider.
Notify the onsite contact of any material, access or site readiness issues and any incomplete work items.
Confirm completion with the onsite contact before leaving site.
customer_responsibilities: Perform all device configurations and troubleshooting, if required.
Ensure onsite personnel are available to assist with functional validation where required.
Provide escalation contacts for technical, access, hardware and schedule related issues.
Provide approval criteria for completed installation and functional testing.
assumptions: Cable management is required.
Functional testing will be performed before the technician leaves the site.
Onsite parking is available; any parking fee is reimbursable.
exclusions: Disposal, recycling, shipping or offsite removal of legacy equipment.
Inventory reconciliation beyond basic identification of the equipment for the installation.
POS application programming (menus, product database, pricing or tax configuration).
Troubleshooting or repair of the customer's internet service provider infrastructure.
Return visits caused by missing equipment, unavailable site access or contacts, or customer-directed schedule changes.
deliverable_outcomes: Installed devices connected, powered and functionally tested.
Completion photos of each installed location.
Notes on material, access or site readiness issues and incomplete work items encountered onsite.
Completion confirmed with the onsite contact.

low_voltage_cabling._source: owner standards loop 2026-10-18: generic cabling handling from the 010082 v1 TEMPLATE list (job-specific hardware left to the deal)
method_steps: Review the work areas and the cable pathway with the onsite point of contact.
Confirm each mounting and termination location with the onsite point of contact before drilling or mounting equipment.
Use fastening methods suited to the existing wall and stud conditions, with anchors or toggle bolts where approved and no stud is available.
Maintain proper cable support and never rest cable directly on ceiling tiles, electrical fixtures, plumbing or ductwork.
Terminate and label each cable run at both ends.
Test each cable run for 4-pair continuity.
Inform the onsite point of contact of each cable's location.
Clean the immediate work area and remove Provider-generated installation debris.
Confirm completion with the onsite contact before leaving site.
customer_responsibilities: Provide device and termination locations before the technician arrives.
assumptions: The work can be completed from an appropriate A-frame ladder; powered lifts, scaffolding or specialty access equipment are not included and may require a change order.
deliverable_outcomes: Cable runs installed, terminated and labeled at both ends.
Continuity test results for each run.
Completion photographs of terminations and visible cable routing.

cameras_security._source: owner standards loop 2026-10-18: generic camera handling from the 010043 v1 TEMPLATE list
method_steps: Coordinate with the customer or authorized representative to confirm final camera placement before mounting.
Route, dress and secure cabling in a professional manner where accessible.
Terminate and label each cable run at the camera location and the IDF.
Mount each camera at its confirmed location.
Connect each camera to the network infrastructure in the IDF.
Verify that each camera powers on and has network connectivity.
Confirm completion with the onsite contact before leaving site.
assumptions: Existing pathways are accessible and usable for each cable run.
The IDF is accessible and has a usable pathway to each camera location.
Lift requirements, if needed, will be handled through a change request.
Any required permits, building or landlord approvals will be handled by the customer unless otherwise stated.
exclusions: Advanced camera analytics configuration.
Work above inaccessible ceilings, in hazardous areas, or in areas requiring special access equipment.
Electrical work.
Camera licensing, cloud portal administration or video management configuration.
After-hours work unless previously approved.
deliverable_outcomes: Cameras mounted at the confirmed locations.
Cable terminations labeled at both ends.
Power and network connectivity verified for each camera.

network_switch_refresh._source: owner standards loop 2026-10-18: generic switch-refresh handling from the 010083 v1 TEMPLATE list
method_steps: Review the existing switch location, rack layout, cabling and available rack space.
Install the new switches in the existing rack, cabinet or customer-designated network area.
Move cables to the new switches one-for-one where practical.
Stage the removed legacy switches onsite in a customer-designated area.
Confirm completion with the onsite contact or remote engineer before leaving site.
customer_responsibilities: Provide the switch configuration before onsite installation.
Provide rack ears, power supplies, power cords, stack cables, optics, patch cables, rack hardware and any other materials required for installation, where applicable.
Perform final network validation, connectivity testing and acceptance testing.
Identify the customer-designated area where removed legacy switches should be staged.
Confirm any site-specific requirements where a dedicated rack is not available or the existing rack, cabinet, cabling or layout may affect the installation.
assumptions: Provider's role is limited to onsite physical labor and field support.
Provider is not responsible for switch configuration, programming, network engineering or final network acceptance.
Removed legacy switches will be left onsite in a customer-designated area.
exclusions: Switch configuration and programming.
Network troubleshooting.
Return logistics for removed equipment.
Structured cabling installation, cable certification, electrical work, rack replacement or circuit troubleshooting unless added by written change order.
deliverable_outcomes: New switches installed and cabled one-for-one where practical.
Removed switches staged onsite in the designated area.
Completion confirmed with the onsite contact or remote engineer.

av_conference_room._source: owner standards loop 2026-10-18: generic AV display handling from the 010217 v1 TEMPLATE list
method_steps: Review each intended display mounting location with the onsite contact before installation.
Inspect existing display mounts and confirm they suit the new display size, weight and VESA pattern before reuse.
Install plywood backing as required to securely support each wall mount.
Mount each display at the approved location and height.
Dress and secure accessible cabling associated with each display.
Connect accessible power where a Customer-provided power source is available.
Power on each display and verify basic operation and an available video source.
Confirm completion with the onsite contact before leaving site.
customer_responsibilities: Provide all displays, hardware, cables and mounts.
Ensure the work areas are reasonably clear and accessible before technician arrival.
Provide access to existing electrical power required for display operation.
Ensure Customer-furnished AV, network and source systems are operational and available for testing.
Provide the final display locations and mounting heights before drilling or permanent installation.
Provide current photographs of the rooms and proposed mounting walls before deployment when available.
assumptions: Mounting walls can structurally support the displays, mounts and backing materials.
Standard commercial wall construction and fastening methods can be used.
No asbestos, hazardous materials, concealed utilities or structural obstructions are present in the work areas.
exclusions: AV system programming, control system configuration or network configuration.
Electrical work or new power circuits.
deliverable_outcomes: Displays mounted at the approved locations and heights.
Power-on and video-source verification for each display.
Completion confirmed with the onsite contact.

relocation_move._source: owner standards loop 2026-10-18: generic relocation handling from the 010147 v1 TEMPLATE list (transport mode and audit/ITAD items are deal facts, left out)
method_steps: Safely pack all equipment designated for relocation, labeling each package.
Coordinate transportation of the packed equipment from the origin location to the designated destination.
Document proof of delivery by photographing the sealed container and its security tag.
Confirm completion with the onsite contact before leaving site.
customer_responsibilities: Power down all equipment before the technicians arrive.
Unrack all applicable devices before packing begins.
Centralize all equipment in an accessible staging area.
Ensure the equipment is ready for packing and transportation during the scheduled service window.
assumptions: No equipment requires a ladder or lift to remove.
exclusions: Furniture, shelving or white boards.
Powering down, disconnecting or unracking equipment at the origin location.
Installation, configuration, cabling or activation of equipment at the destination unless added by written change order.
deliverable_outcomes: Equipment packed and labeled for transport.
Proof-of-delivery photographs of the sealed container and security tag.
Completion confirmed with the onsite contact.
